title: [Docs] CHANGELOG, architecture.md and native plugin comments contradict the code on HTTP/2 over SslStream, ProjectJsonBridge and importer constraints
body:
## Summary
CHANGELOG.md says TurboHTTP.Transport runs HTTP/2 over SslStream and omits TurboHTTP.UniTask.WebSocket, while README.md and Transport.md say SslStream has no ALPN and HTTP/2 needs BouncyCastle. architecture.md:37 says Auth reaches JSON through reflection, but ProjectJsonBridge is a registration slot. The iOS and Android background plugin sources claim importer define constraints gate them, while TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate records that Unity 2021.3 does not apply them. CLAUDE.md calls the package commercial while package.json and LICENSE.md are MIT. Readers get wrong guidance about the module list, HTTP/2 prerequisites and plugin gating.

## Location
- `CHANGELOG.md:28`

## Problem
CHANGELOG.md:28-29 describes TurboHTTP.Transport as 'raw-socket HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 over SslStream', while README.md:12 and Documentation~/Modules/Transport.md:20-21 state that Unity's SslStream has no ALPN and HTTP/2 needs the BouncyCastle backend; the module list (:28-36) names TurboHTTP.UniTask but not the shipped TurboHTTP.UniTask.WebSocket (Runtime/UniTask.WebSocket/TurboHTTP.UniTask.WebSocket.asmdef) nor TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol's always-compiled status (finding 04). Development~/docs/agents/architecture.md:37 says 'Auth reaches JSON through reflection (ProjectJsonBridge), a hidden dependency (#67)', but ProjectJsonBridge is a registration slot with no by-name lookup (Runtime/Core/ProjectJsonBridge.cs:11-13, 28-31) and Runtime/JSON/link.xml:3-5 says so. Plugins/iOS/TurboHttpBackgroundTaskBridge.mm:5-7 and Plugins/Android/TurboHttpBackground.androidlib/AndroidManifest.xml:2-3 say Unity includes the plugin 'only when the TURBOHTTP_BACKGROUND_NETWORKING scripting define is set (importer define constraint)', while Editor/TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate.cs:16-19 records that Unity 2021.3 does not apply importer define constraints to native plugins and the include delegate is what gates them. CLAUDE.md line 3 calls the package 'commercial' while package.json:23, LICENSE.md and Third-Party Notices.md:3 are MIT (consistent with each other).

**Failure scenario.** An integrator reading the changelog expects HTTP/2 from the default install and files a bug when ALPN never selects h2; an agent following architecture.md treats ProjectJsonBridge as a reflection site and adds link.xml rules for it (the pattern finding 01 describes); a maintainer who trusts the .mm comment removes the Editor gate and ships the background plugins into every build.

## Suggested fix
Correct the three changelog statements, replace architecture.md:37 with the registration description, and reword the plugin comments to name TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate as the mechanism.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md states that HTTP/2 needs the BouncyCastle backend, lists TurboHTTP.UniTask.WebSocket and notes TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol's compile status
- [ ] Development~/docs/agents/architecture.md:37 describes the ProjectJsonBridge registration slot, not reflection
- [ ] TurboHttpBackgroundTaskBridge.mm and the androidlib AndroidManifest.xml comments name TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate as the gating mechanism
- [ ] CLAUDE.md licence wording matches package.json and LICENSE.md

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `pkg-pluggability-17` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/pkg.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: docs.

Verification: Not independently verified: low-severity findings were not sent to a second reviewer. Re-trace it in the code before fixing.

title: [Packaging] TurboHttpLinkerProcessor applies every compiled module's link.xml, so rules naming TurboHTTP types root optional modules in all stripped players
body:
## Summary
The linker processor decides that a module is in the build by checking that its DLL exists in the linker input. Every runtime asmdef except the define-gated ones always compiles, so all link.xml rules apply even when a project never uses the module. The audit finds 32 of 44 type rules protect code nothing reaches by reflection, and the named assemblies' [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod] hooks become roots too. Stripped players keep far more first-party code than a minimal HTTP/1.1 client needs.

## Location
- `Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.cs:149`

## Problem
TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.CreateAssemblyProbe (Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.cs:83-92) answers 'in build' with File.Exists(inputDirectory/<name>.dll), and BuildMergedLinkXml skips a link.xml only when that is false (:148-150). Every runtime asmdef except the two define-gated ones (Transport.BouncyCastle, UniTask*) has empty defineConstraints and compiles for every non-WebGL player, so its DLL is always in the linker input and its rules always apply, whether or not the project uses the module. Rule audit (44 type rules in 9 files): Runtime/Unity/link.xml:2-13 preserves 10 decoder types 'all' in TurboHTTP.Unity, but DecoderRegistry.AddDefaultDecoders_NoLock constructs them with plain 'new' (Runtime/Unity/Decoders/DecoderRegistry.cs:417-425); no reflection. Naming the assembly makes UnityLinker process an assembly that nothing else references, and RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethodAttribute derives from PreserveAttribute (noted in Tests/Runtime/Transport/TransportBootstrapTests.cs:52-53), so the module's 11 startup hooks become roots too (MainThreadDispatcher.cs:218/242, UnityTempFileManager.cs:108/414, AudioClipHandler.cs:109/123, TextureDecodeScheduler.cs:97, LifecycleCancellation.cs:114, StreamedAudioTempFiles.cs:62, DecoderRegistry.cs:75, AndroidBackgroundExpirySignal.cs:85). Runtime/JSON/link.xml:9-12 preserves JsonExtensions and JsonSerializer 'all' while its own comment says no TurboHTTP assembly looks them up by name. Runtime/Transport/link.xml:64-69 preserves RawSocketTransport, Http2ResponseBodySource, SingleReaderChannel`1 and TransportModuleInitializer 'all' (static call sites only). Runtime/WebSocket.Transport/link.xml:8-11 preserves RawSocketWebSocketTransport 'all'. Runtime/Core/link.xml:7-15 preserves 4 Core types and IAsyncDisposable (all statically used). Runtime/Observability/link.xml:9-12 preserves StackTrace/StackFrame 'all' for a direct 'new StackTrace(...)' call that is compiled only under DEBUG || TURBOHTTP_POOL_DIAGNOSTICS (PooledBuffer.cs:63-70). Runtime/Testing/link.xml:7-16 (5 BCL crypto types) and Runtime/WebSocket/link.xml:9-13 (3 BCL crypto types) are by-name provider lookups and justified, but they are applied to every player because TurboHTTP.Testing.dll and TurboHTTP.WebSocket.dll always compile. Only the #450 configuration rules (Transport/link.xml:30-43, 4 rules) and those 8 BCL crypto rules protect real reflection. A repo-wide search of Runtime/ (outside Lib/) for GetType(string)/GetMethod/GetField/Activator/MakeGeneric finds only JsonUtilitySerializer.cs:362 (GetFields on user DTOs) and Core/IL2CPPCompatibility.cs:91 (self-test). Tests/Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessorTests.cs:42-53 ('MergedLinkXml_PreservesReflectionTarget') asserts the JSON/Transport/WebSocket.Transport rules as required 'reflection targets', i.e. the test pins the over-rooting.

**Failure scenario.** A project that only does 'new UHttpClient().Get(url)' builds for Android IL2CPP at Managed Stripping Level Medium. The merged Temp/TurboHTTP/TurboHTTP.link.xml names TurboHTTP.Unity, so the linker keeps the decoders (including the three always-throwing stubs, #158) plus every hook-rooted type; at startup the player creates the '[TurboHTTP MainThreadDispatcher]' DontDestroyOnLoad GameObject, installs a PlayerLoop system and reads Application.temporaryCachePath, although no TurboHTTP.Unity API is used. At Minimal (per the Unity manual the IL2CPP default in 2021.3, where non-engine assemblies in the closure are copied whole) the whole 9.1 KLOC TurboHTTP.Unity assembly is kept. The documented claim 'Each module's rules apply only when that module's assembly is in the build' (Documentation~/PlatformNotes.md:187) is true only for the two define-gated modules.

## Suggested fix
Delete the link.xml rules that name TurboHTTP types (Unity, JSON, Core, the four Transport types, WebSocket.Transport) and where a root is really wanted use an in-assembly PreserveAttribute, which only takes effect once the assembly is otherwise reachable. Keep link.xml for BCL by-name targets only, and move the Testing/WebSocket crypto rules behind something that reflects use (for example a [Preserve]d static reference is not possible for BCL types, so keep them but document that they are unconditional). Rename the test to assert that no rule names a TurboHTTP assembly other than the define-gated BouncyCastle glue. Do finding 03 first: the Android cleartext hook currently survives only because of this over-rooting.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] link.xml rules that name TurboHTTP types are removed or replaced by in-assembly PreserveAttribute where a root is genuinely needed; link.xml keeps only BCL by-name targets
- [ ] Testing and WebSocket crypto rules apply only when the owning module is reachable
- [ ] A minimal HTTP/1.1 GET + JSON IL2CPP player no longer links Unity, Testing or WebSocket.Transport types (measured with the linker dependency report and recorded)
- [ ] Editor test under Tests/Editor/ asserts the merged link.xml contains no rule naming an optional module's types

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `pkg-pluggability-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/pkg.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: Code is as described. Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.cs:83-92 answers 'in build' with File.Exists(<inputDirectory>/<name>.dll) and :148-150 skips a link.xml only on false; every runtime asmdef except Transport.BouncyCastle and the two UniTask ones has empty defineConstraints, so only those are ever skipped. Rule count is right (44 type rules in 9 files). Runtime/Unity/link.xml:2-13 preserves 10 decoder types 'all' while DecoderRegistry.cs:417-425 constructs them with plain new; the only reflection in Runtime/ outside Lib/ is JsonUtilitySerializer.cs:362 and IL2CPPCompatibility.cs:91. PooledBuffer.cs:63-69 is the only StackTrace use. Repo evidence supports the mechanism: Development~/docs/implementation-journal/2026-11-player-build-smoke.md:67 lists the android-il2cpp High output as Auth, Complete, Core, JSON, Retry, Transport, Unity, WebSocket, WebSocket.Transport, i.e. unreferenced package assemblies (Observability, which has a [Preserve] RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod at ObservabilityModuleRegistration.cs:23-25, Cache, Files, Middleware, RateLimit, Testing) are dropped, so an assembly named by link.xml is what keeps an otherwise unreferenced module. Not settled statically: that smoke project uses TurboHTTP.Unity itself (Tools~/unity/player-smoke/TurboHttpPlayerSmoke.cs:27), so no recorded build shows a Core-only project, and whether UnityLinker then also roots the module's 11 startup hooks depends on linker behaviour. Scope is narrower than the title: only TurboHTTP.Unity is newly rooted by these rules; JSON, Transport and WebSocket.Transport are already rooted by the always-linked Complete bootstrap (TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:53-54, 89-90; finding 02), where the rules only add members; the Testing and WebSocket link.xml name BCL types only and root no TurboHTTP module (Auth and Unity/PathSafety.cs:161 also rely on those unconditional crypto rules). In unstripped Mono players all hooks run anyway, so the cost is size and startup work in stripped builds, not wrong behaviour. PlatformNotes.md:187 is literally true ('assembly is in the build' = compiled). Removing the Unity rules would expose finding 03.

Related: #35, #258.

title: [Packaging] TurboHttpWebGlBuildGuard fails every WebGL build of a project that has the package installed, with no opt-out
body:
## Summary
TurboHttpWebGlBuildGuard.OnPreprocessBuild throws BuildFailedException for any WebGL build, without checking whether the build uses TurboHTTP. Multi-target projects cannot remove the package per platform, and HttpTransportFactory.Register is a public extension point for an application-supplied browser transport. Source comments (ProjectJsonBridge, JsonModuleRegistration, WebSocketTransportFactory) and APIReference.md still describe a WebGL path, so code and docs disagree.

## Location
- `Editor/TurboHttpWebGlBuildGuard.cs:31`

## Problem
TurboHttpWebGlBuildGuard.OnPreprocessBuild throws BuildFailedException whenever report.summary.platform == BuildTarget.WebGL (Editor/TurboHttpWebGlBuildGuard.cs:23-33); there is no define, setting or check of whether the build uses TurboHTTP. The message's remedy is 'remove the TurboHTTP package from WebGL projects' (:15-18), which a multi-target project cannot do per platform. Meanwhile Core, JSON, Middleware, Auth, Retry, Cache, RateLimit, Observability, Files, Testing, Unity, WebSocket and Unity.WebSocket do not exclude WebGL (only Transport, WebSocket.Transport, Complete and the BouncyCastle pair do), and the sources still tell WebGL users what to call: ProjectJsonBridge.cs:8-10 ('WebGL builds (which exclude it too), call JsonModuleRegistration.EnsureRegistered()'), JsonModuleRegistration.cs:13-14 ('it is excluded on WebGL'), WebSocketTransportFactory.cs:31-34 ('the platform must not be WebGL'), Documentation~/APIReference.md:191. HttpTransportFactory.Register is public, so a browser transport supplied by the application is a supported extension point that the guard makes unbuildable. Tests/Editor/WebGlBuildGuardTests.cs:21-29 only pins the unconditional failure.

**Failure scenario.** A game ships on iOS, Android (TurboHTTP) and WebGL (its own UnityWebRequest path behind #if UNITY_WEBGL, or a custom IHttpTransport over fetch registered with HttpTransportFactory.Register). After installing the package the WebGL target fails at build time with 'TurboHTTP does not support WebGL in v1.0'; the only fixes are forking the package or a CI step that edits Packages/manifest.json before WebGL builds.

## Suggested fix
Keep the fail-fast default but add an escape hatch: skip the guard when a scripting define such as TURBOHTTP_ALLOW_WEBGL_BUILD is set for the WebGL target (or downgrade to a build warning when the application registered a transport), state it in the error text and PlatformNotes, and test both branches. Align the stale 'excluded on WebGL' comments with whichever behaviour is chosen.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The guard can be disabled by a documented scripting define (for example TURBOHTTP_ALLOW_WEBGL_BUILD) or downgrades to a warning when an application transport is registered
- [ ] The error text and PlatformNotes name the opt-out
- [ ] Stale comments about WebGL exclusion match the chosen behaviour
- [ ] Editor test in Tests/Editor/WebGlBuildGuardTests.cs covers both the failing and the opted-out branch

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `pkg-pluggability-07` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/pkg.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: platform-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: TurboHttpWebGlBuildGuard.OnPreprocessBuild throws BuildFailedException for every WebGL build (Editor/TurboHttpWebGlBuildGuard.cs:23-33) with no define, setting or check of whether the build uses TurboHTTP; the message's remedy is to remove the package (:14-18). Tests/Editor/WebGlBuildGuardTests.cs:21-29 pins the unconditional failure. The guard is deliberate (#9, closed; WebGL transport is #130, v2.0) and documented (README.md:148, PlatformNotes.md:14, QuickStart.md:9), so this is not an accident. Its stated reason ('every request would fail at runtime') does not hold for a multi-target project that keeps TurboHTTP out of its WebGL code path or registers its own transport: HttpTransportFactory.Register is public and Runtime/Core/IHttpTransport.cs:10 names 'WebGL browser fetch' as a reason to replace the transport. #9's own acceptance criterion allowed the alternative 'or compiles nothing from TurboHTTP'. Core, JSON, Unity, WebSocket and the other modules still compile for WebGL, and comments still describe a WebGL path that cannot be built: ProjectJsonBridge.cs:8-9, JsonModuleRegistration.cs:13-14, WebSocketTransportFactory.cs:31-34, HttpTransportFactory.cs:164-165, APIReference.md:191. No opt-out exists in the repository and no open issue covers one.

Related: #130.

title: [Mobile] Android background plugin Gradle module uses manifest package and lintOptions with no namespace, which AGP 8 (Unity 6) rejects
body:
## Summary
Plugins/Android/TurboHttpBackground.androidlib sets package in AndroidManifest.xml and declares no namespace in build.gradle, and it uses the deprecated lintOptions block. Android Gradle Plugin 8 requires the namespace in the module build file. The package advertises Unity 2021.3+, so a Unity 6 project that defines TURBOHTTP_BACKGROUND_NETWORKING fails the Android Gradle configuration.

## Location
- `Plugins/Android/TurboHttpBackground.androidlib/AndroidManifest.xml:6`

## Problem
Plugins/Android/TurboHttpBackground.androidlib/AndroidManifest.xml:5-6 sets package="com.turbohttp.background"; build.gradle:10-32 has an android { } block with compileSdkVersion, defaultConfig, sourceSets and 'lintOptions { abortOnError false }' (:29-31) but no 'namespace'. AGP 8 requires the namespace in the module's build file and fails when it is supplied only through the manifest's package attribute; lintOptions is the deprecated spelling of lint. package.json:5 says unity 2021.3 (a minimum) and README.md:3 and :25 say 'Unity 2021.3+'. The plugin is opt-in (TURBOHTTP_BACKGROUND_NETWORKING) and experimental, and Tools~/ci/check_repo.py does not inspect the .androidlib (NATIVE_SOURCES, :497).

**Failure scenario.** A project on Unity 6 (AGP 8.x) defines TURBOHTTP_BACKGROUND_NETWORKING for Android. Gradle configuration of the :unityLibrary:TurboHttpBackground.androidlib module fails with 'Namespace not specified' / 'package attribute in AndroidManifest.xml is no longer supported', so the Android build fails. Not confirmable statically: needs one Android build on Unity 2022.3 and one on Unity 6 with the define set.

## Suggested fix
Declare the namespace in build.gradle when the AGP in use supports it (for example 'if (android.hasProperty("namespace")) namespace "com.turbohttp.background"'), keep the manifest attribute only for AGP 4, switch to the 'lint' block the same way, and record the supported editor range for the experimental plugin in PlatformNotes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] build.gradle declares the namespace when the AGP supports it and uses the lint block on AGP 8, while AGP 4 still builds
- [ ] PlatformNotes records the supported Unity/AGP range of the experimental plugin
- [ ] One Android build on Unity 2022.3 and one on Unity 6 with the define set succeed and the result is validated on a device and recorded
- [ ] check_repo.py inspects the .androidlib for a namespace declaration (Tests/ or Tools~/ci check)

## Context

title: [Architecture] Auth, Cache, Files, Middleware, Retry, RateLimit and Testing asmdefs keep noEngineReferences false and are not in check_repo ENGINE_FREE
body:
## Summary
Seven modules contain no use of UnityEngine, UnityEditor or UNITY_ symbols but their asmdefs set noEngineReferences to false. check_repo.py ENGINE_FREE lists only Transport, SecureProtocol, JSON, WebSocket and WebSocket.Transport, so nothing prevents engine calls from creeping into these 56 files. The non-Unity harnesses under Tools~ could then no longer load them.

## Location
- `Runtime/Auth/TurboHTTP.Auth.asmdef:13`

## Problem
'noEngineReferences: false' at line 13 of TurboHTTP.Auth.asmdef, .Cache, .Files, .Middleware, .Retry, .RateLimit and .Testing asmdefs. A search of each module for UnityEngine, UnityEditor or UNITY_ finds 0 files in Auth (10 files), Cache (12), Files (5), Middleware (11), Retry (4), RateLimit (4) and Testing (10); Observability (2 files) and Core (6 files) do use the engine. Tools~/ci/check_repo.py:63 ENGINE_FREE lists only Transport, SecureProtocol, JSON, WebSocket and WebSocket.Transport, matching architecture.md's table, so nothing stops engine calls from creeping into these 56 files.

**Failure scenario.** A later change adds Debug.Log or Application.persistentDataPath to the Cache or Files module; it compiles and passes CI, the module now needs the main thread or an engine module on a worker-thread path, and the non-Unity harnesses under Tools~ (which link these assemblies on plain .NET) lose the ability to load it. Today each of these assemblies is also compiled against the full UnityEngine reference set for no reason.

## Suggested fix
Set noEngineReferences: true on the seven asmdefs, add them to ENGINE_FREE in check_repo.py and to the architecture table. This is a one-line change per file with no API impact.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] noEngineReferences is true in the seven asmdefs and the package still compiles
- [ ] check_repo.py ENGINE_FREE and the architecture.md table include the seven modules
- [ ] check_repo fails when a UnityEngine reference is added to one of them (Tools~/ci check or Tests/Editor/ test)

## Context

title: [Packaging] ObservabilityModuleRegistration registers the Editor monitor hook in players, rooting MonitorInterceptor, MonitorHandler and HttpMonitorEvent
body:
## Summary
EnsureRegistered carries [Preserve] and [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod] with no #if and constructs MonitorInterceptor, but the only consumer of the hook (UHttpClient.TryAppendEditorMonitorInterceptor) exists under UNITY_EDITOR. In a player that uses any other Observability type, the linker keeps about 1,400 of the module's 2,965 lines and the method runs at every start for a factory nobody calls.

## Location
- `Runtime/Observability/ObservabilityModuleRegistration.cs:24`

## Problem
ObservabilityModuleRegistration.EnsureRegistered carries [Preserve] and [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(SubsystemRegistration)] with no #if (Runtime/Observability/ObservabilityModuleRegistration.cs:23-28) and registers CreateMonitorInterceptor, which constructs MonitorInterceptor (:30-44). The hook is read only by UHttpClient.TryAppendEditorMonitorInterceptor, which exists under '#if UNITY_EDITOR' (Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:794-796 and 801-830); in a player EditorMonitorHook.TryAppend is never called. MonitorInterceptor.cs is 943 lines, MonitorHandler.cs 163, HttpMonitorEvent.cs 312. The assembly has no AlwaysLinkAssembly, so the root takes effect whenever the linker processes TurboHTTP.Observability for another reason, for example the project uses LoggingInterceptor or MetricsInterceptor.

**Failure scenario.** A game adds only MetricsInterceptor to its client. In the IL2CPP player the linker processes TurboHTTP.Observability, keeps EnsureRegistered because of [Preserve], and through it the whole monitor capture path (ring buffer, redaction, body snapshots); the method also runs at every player start to register a factory nobody will call. Roughly half of the module's code is dead weight in that build.

## Suggested fix
Compile the attribute pair (or the whole method body and the class's player-side root) under #if UNITY_EDITOR; keep the public EnsureRegistered for explicit use. The Editor monitor window reaches MonitorInterceptor directly, so nothing in players changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The [Preserve] and startup attribute pair (or the method body) is compiled under UNITY_EDITOR; public EnsureRegistered remains for explicit use
- [ ] An IL2CPP player using only MetricsInterceptor no longer links MonitorInterceptor, MonitorHandler or HttpMonitorEvent (measured and recorded)
- [ ] The Editor monitor window still works (Tests/Editor/ test)

## Context

title: [Packaging] TurboHTTP.Testing has no define or platform constraint, so it ships in every unstripped Mono player and its link.xml crypto rules always apply
body:
## Summary
TurboHTTP.Testing (mock server, record/replay, 10 files, 3,343 lines) has empty includePlatforms, excludePlatforms and defineConstraints. Mono release builds with stripping disabled copy TurboHTTP.Testing.dll, and every stripped build merges its link.xml that preserves five BCL crypto types. Games that never use MockTransport ship test infrastructure.

## Location
- `Runtime/Testing/TurboHTTP.Testing.asmdef:11`

## Problem
Runtime/Testing/TurboHTTP.Testing.asmdef:5-6 and :11 have empty includePlatforms, excludePlatforms and defineConstraints (only autoReferenced: false, :10), so the assembly compiles for every player. With the Mono backend's default stripping (Disabled) all compiled assemblies are copied, including TurboHTTP.Testing.dll with its System.Linq (4 files), Regex (1 file) and SHA-256/HMAC use. On IL2CPP it is dropped when unreferenced, but Runtime/Testing/link.xml:7-16 (SHA256, SHA256Managed, HMACSHA256, RNGCryptoServiceProvider, SHA256CryptoServiceProvider, all preserve=all) is merged whenever the DLL is in the linker input, i.e. always (Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.cs:148-150). The assembly is also listed in TurboHTTP.Complete.asmdef:16.

**Failure scenario.** A Standalone or Android Mono release build of a game that never uses MockTransport ships the mock transport, the record/replay file format reader/writer and its redaction code as loadable managed code, and every IL2CPP build keeps five BCL crypto types fully preserved on behalf of a module it does not contain.

## Suggested fix
Decide the intended audience: if Testing is for tests and development only, constrain the asmdef (for example 'UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS || DEVELOPMENT_BUILD || UNITY_EDITOR || TURBOHTTP_TESTING_IN_PLAYER') and note it in the changelog as breaking; otherwise at least drop it from Complete's references and make its link.xml rules conditional on the assembly being referenced (see finding 01).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The audience of the module is decided and documented; if development-only, the asmdef is constrained (for example UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS || DEVELOPMENT_BUILD || UNITY_EDITOR) and the change is noted in the changelog
- [ ] TurboHTTP.Complete no longer pulls Testing into release players or the reference is documented
- [ ] A release Mono player build does not contain TurboHTTP.Testing.dll (verified and recorded)
- [ ] Editor test in Tests/Editor/ asserts the asmdef constraint

## Context

title: [Core] Shipped assemblies grant InternalsVisibleTo to four unshipped dev harness assemblies, exposing internals and the TLS test trust-anchor seam by name
body:
## Summary
Runtime/Transport/AssemblyInfo.cs and Runtime/Core/AssemblyInfo.cs name TurboHTTP.Soak, TlsInterop, H2Interop and Fuzz unconditionally. Unity assemblies are not strong-named, so any asmdef with one of those names compiles against Core and Transport internals, including ServerCertificateVerifier.AddTestTrustAnchor, which adds a process-wide extra root for the BouncyCastle path.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/AssemblyInfo.cs:7`

## Problem
Runtime/Transport/AssemblyInfo.cs:7, 9, 11, 13 name TurboHTTP.TlsInterop, TurboHTTP.H2Interop, TurboHTTP.Fuzz and TurboHTTP.Soak ('Tools~/..., not shipped'); Runtime/Core/AssemblyInfo.cs:19 names TurboHTTP.Soak, next to 14 module assemblies and the test assembly (:3-17). The attributes are unconditional and Unity assemblies are not strong-named, so the friend relation is by simple name. Among the internals this exposes is ServerCertificateVerifier.AddTestTrustAnchor / RestoreTestTrustAnchors (Runtime/Transport/Tls/ServerCertificateVerifier.cs:303-334), which makes the BouncyCastle path validate against an extra root process-wide (:286-291).

**Failure scenario.** A third-party package in the same project names its asmdef 'TurboHTTP.Fuzz'. It compiles against every internal type of TurboHTTP.Transport and can call AddTestTrustAnchor without reflection, surviving stripping because the reference is static. This widens the boundary breach #76 tracks (which counted 10 friends) with names the package does not even ship.

## Suggested fix
Emit the harness friend attributes only in harness builds (#if TURBOHTTP_DEV_HARNESS, defined by the Tools~ project files), and keep the shipped list to shipped assemblies plus the test assembly. Compile the test trust-anchor seam under the same symbol or UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Harness friend attributes are emitted only under a harness define (for example TURBOHTTP_DEV_HARNESS set by Tools~ projects); the shipped list names only shipped assemblies and the test assembly
- [ ] AddTestTrustAnchor and RestoreTestTrustAnchors are compiled only for tests or harness builds
- [ ] Harness projects under Tools~ still build (check.sh --full)
- [ ] Test in Tests/Editor/ asserts the shipped assemblies' InternalsVisibleTo list

title: [Packaging] Vendored TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol asmdef has no define constraint, so BouncyCastle (138,572 lines) ships in every unstripped Mono player
body:
## Summary
The vendored BouncyCastle asmdef has defineConstraints [], so Unity compiles it for every non-WebGL target; only the glue asmdef is gated by TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE. On Mono with Managed Stripping Level Disabled all compiled assemblies are copied, so TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol.dll ships with the define off, contradicting CHANGELOG.md:108-110. The asmdef is TurboHTTP-owned and survives the re-vendor sync, and CI never builds the define-off configuration.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/Lib/TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol.asmdef:13`

## Problem
Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/Lib/TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol.asmdef:13 'defineConstraints: []' (only the glue asmdef carries TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE, TurboHTTP.Transport.BouncyCastle.asmdef:17-19); no file under Lib/ contains the define (0 of 681). Unity therefore compiles the library for every non-WebGL target. On IL2CPP nothing references it without the glue, so UnityLinker drops it; on the Mono backend the default Managed Stripping Level is Disabled, UnityLinker does not run, and every compiled player assembly is copied to Managed/, including TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol.dll. CHANGELOG.md:108-110 states 'Without the define ... the BouncyCastle assemblies are not linked into player builds', and Tests/Editor/ModuleAutoReferenceTests.cs:75-81 asserts only the glue's constraint with the comment 'neither assembly reaches a player's linker output'. #258 records that the asmdef is unconstrained but reasons 'CLAUDE.md marks Lib/ as never-write' and 'we expect UnityLinker to drop it': the asmdef is not vendored content (the re-vendor rsync excludes it, Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/README.md:19-23), and the Mono/Disabled case is not considered. Tools~/ci/shadow_build.py:70-76 puts TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE (and TURBOHTTP_BACKGROUND_NETWORKING) in COMMON_DEFINES for every variant and Tools~/unity/run-tests.sh writes the define into the test project (#258 text), so no gate compiles the configuration most customers use. Related always-on cost of the opt-in backend: the BouncyCastle-only verifier stack lives in TurboHTTP.Transport (ServerCertificateVerifier 477, WindowsCertificateVerifier 445, MacSecTrustVerifier 346, PlatformCertificateVerifier 249, AppleTrustVerifier 182 lines; only callers are in Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/), and Plugins/iOS/TurboHttpSecTrustVerifier.mm.meta has 'defineConstraints: []' with no include gate, so the native verifier is compiled into every iOS build.

**Failure scenario.** A Windows or Android Mono player built from a project that never sets TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE contains TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol.dll (a TLS 1.2/1.3 stack, X.509 and elliptic-curve code, in the order of megabytes of IL) that no code can call; every fresh import, platform switch and CI build also compiles 138 KLOC for nothing. A customer auditing the build against the changelog's 'not linked into player builds' finds a crypto library they were told is absent, which also matters for export-compliance questionnaires.

## Suggested fix
Add defineConstraints ['TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE'] to Lib/TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol.asmdef (the asmdef is TurboHTTP-owned and survives the re-vendor sync) and assert it in ModuleAutoReferenceTests and check_repo. Correct CHANGELOG.md:108-110 until then. Add a shadow-build pass without the two opt-in defines. Longer term move the verifier stack and the iOS .mm behind the same define (they are useless without the provider).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol.asmdef has defineConstraints [TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE]; ModuleAutoReferenceTests and check_repo assert it
- [ ] A Mono player built without the define does not contain TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol.dll (verified and recorded)
- [ ] The shadow build gains a pass without the opt-in defines (Tools~/ci/shadow_build.py)
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md:108-110 is accurate

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `pkg-pluggability-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/pkg.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/Lib/TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol.asmdef has defineConstraints [] and no file under Lib/ contains the define; only the glue asmdef is gated. The repo's own records confirm the outcome: Tools~/unity/build-player.sh:26-29 and :392-397 assert SecureProtocol absent at Stripping High only ('Mono Disabled copies every compiled assembly'), and 2026-11-player-build-smoke.md:64 records 'win64-mono, no BC ... TurboHTTP.SecureProtocol.dll copied'. So CHANGELOG.md:108-110 ('the BouncyCastle assemblies are not linked into player builds') is false for the default Mono configuration, and the comment at Tests/Editor/ModuleAutoReferenceTests.cs:77-78 overstates. Tools~/ci/shadow_build.py:70-76 puts TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE in COMMON_DEFINES, so no gate compiles the define-off configuration. #258 tracks the unconstrained asmdef, but its 2nd comment closes the question with 'stripped under High ... needs no define constraint', which covers IL2CPP High only; the Mono Disabled (and below-High) case is known to the tooling and accepted without an issue, so #258 understates it. The asmdef is TurboHTTP-owned: the re-vendor rsync excludes it (Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/README.md:19-22). Side claims hold: the certificate verifier stack (1,699 lines in Runtime/Transport/Tls) is called only from Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/, and Plugins/iOS/TurboHttpSecTrustVerifier.mm.meta has defineConstraints [] with no Editor gate (the gate covers only the background plugin).

title: [Packaging] Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/link.xml names TurboHTTP.Transport.BouncyCastle without ignoreIfMissing, breaking stripped builds when the package sits under Assets/
body:
## Summary
When the package is copied under Assets/, Unity reads every link.xml itself without the linker processor's filtering. The BouncyCastle link.xml names an assembly that is not compiled without TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE and lacks ignoreIfMissing, so UnityLinker fails with an unresolved-assembly error. Users who import the package as a .unitypackage or copy it into Assets/ are affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/link.xml:15`

## Problem
TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.FindPackageRoot has a branch for 'Copy embedded under Assets/' (Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.cs:66-74), and TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate.IsGatedPlugin matches by path suffix for the same reason (Editor/TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate.cs:65-78). In that layout Unity collects every link.xml under Assets/ on its own, without the processor's filtering. Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/link.xml:15 is '<assembly fullname="TurboHTTP.Transport.BouncyCastle">' with no ignoreIfMissing attribute; the processor adds ignoreIfMissing="1" only to its merged copy (TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.cs:187-191), and its class comment (:22-25) explains why: a rule for an absent assembly fails UnityLinker with an unresolved-assembly error. The glue assembly is not compiled without the define (TurboHTTP.Transport.BouncyCastle.asmdef:17-19). Tests/Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessorTests.cs:93-124 requires ignoreIfMissing only for non-TurboHTTP assembly names.

**Failure scenario.** The package is delivered as a .unitypackage or Asset Store import under Assets/TurboHTTP (planned packaging work, #101) or a user copies it there. An IL2CPP build without TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE passes Assets/TurboHTTP/Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/link.xml to UnityLinker, which cannot resolve TurboHTTP.Transport.BouncyCastle and aborts the build. Confirm with one stripped build of a project that has the package folder under Assets/.

## Suggested fix
Put ignoreIfMissing="1" on every <assembly> element in the source link.xml files whose assembly is define- or platform-gated (at least the BouncyCastle one), and extend PackageLinkXml_FrameworkRulesNameTheImplementingAssembly to require it for assemblies with defineConstraints.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every <assembly> element in the source link.xml files whose assembly is define- or platform-gated, including TurboHTTP.Transport.BouncyCastle, carries ignoreIfMissing="1"
- [ ] PackageLinkXml_FrameworkRulesNameTheImplementingAssembly requires ignoreIfMissing for assemblies with defineConstraints
- [ ] A stripped IL2CPP build without TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE, with the package under Assets/TurboHTTP, completes and is recorded
- [ ] Regression test in Tests/Editor/ fails when a gated assembly rule lacks ignoreIfMissing

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `pkg-pluggability-09` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/pkg.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: platform-compat.

title: [Packaging] RawSocketTransport statically links the full HTTP/2 stack into every player although default Unity runtimes cannot negotiate h2
body:
## Summary
RawSocketTransport creates Http2ConnectionManager unconditionally and the dispatch paths consult it, so about 8,358 lines of HTTP/2 and HPACK code are reachable and linked in every player. Without the opt-in BouncyCastle provider ALPN never selects h2 on Unity runtimes, so that code cannot run. Size-sensitive projects pay for it in every build.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:74`

## Problem
RawSocketTransport's constructor creates 'new Http2ConnectionManager(http2Options, _streamingOptions)' unconditionally (Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:74) and the dispatch paths call _h2Manager.GetIfExists/GetOrCreateAsync (:586, 629, 690, 868, 971, 1137), so Http2Connection (4 partial files, 3,381 lines), Http2Stream (864), Http2ResponseBodySource (689), HpackEncoder/Decoder/Huffman/static and dynamic tables (1,389) and the frame codec are reachable from the default transport. Runtime/Transport/link.xml:65-66 additionally preserves SingleReaderChannel`1 and Http2ResponseBodySource 'all'. The transport's own capability probe says when this code can run: ProbeCapabilities (RawSocketTransport.cs:126-139) reports Http2 only when SslStream supports ALPN, commented 'never on Unity's runtimes', or when the BouncyCastle provider is registered. README.md:12 and Documentation~/Modules/Transport.md:20-21 say the same ('Unity's SslStream has no ALPN, so connections use HTTP/1.1'). There is no h2c/prior-knowledge path (Http2Connection.cs:52 'If h2c is introduced...'). TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE is off by default, so in the default configuration the selection is a runtime branch the linker cannot remove.

**Failure scenario.** Default install, IL2CPP, any stripping level: the player carries the full HTTP/2 + HPACK implementation (Huffman tables, static table, flow control, read loop, pooled streams) and its generic instantiations, none of which can execute because ALPN never selects h2. For the 'HTTP/1.1 GET with JSON' build this is the single largest avoidable block of first-party code: about 8.4 of the roughly 26 KLOC that build actually needs to link next to it.

## Suggested fix
Put HTTP/2 behind a registration seam the linker can cut: an internal IHttp2Dispatcher set by a small TurboHTTP.Transport.Http2 assembly (or a TURBOHTTP_HTTP2 define implied by TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE and by a future native ALPN backend, #429), with RawSocketTransport holding only the interface. Drop the two Http2 link.xml rules. This is the highest-payoff restructuring after the BouncyCastle asmdef constraint, at medium effort because Http2ConnectionManager is constructed and consulted inline today.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] RawSocketTransport references HTTP/2 only through an internal interface registered by a separate assembly or a define-gated module, so the linker can remove the stack when it is not registered
- [ ] The two Http2 rules in Runtime/Transport/link.xml are removed or made conditional
- [ ] A default HTTP/1.1-only build no longer links Http2Connection, Http2Stream and the HPACK types, checked with a linker report and recorded
- [ ] Regression test in Tests/Runtime/Transport/ verifies HTTP/2 is still negotiated when the module is registered and falls back to HTTP/1.1 when it is not

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `pkg-pluggability-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/pkg.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: RawSocketTransport's constructor creates Http2ConnectionManager unconditionally (Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:74) and the dispatch paths consult _h2Manager, so the HTTP/2 stack is statically reachable from the default transport; Runtime/Transport/link.xml:65-66 additionally preserves SingleReaderChannel`1 and Http2ResponseBodySource 'all'. Runtime/Transport/Http2 is 23 files (finding says 22), 8,358 lines, of 21,837 in TurboHTTP.Transport outside BouncyCastle (38%). ProbeCapabilities (RawSocketTransport.cs:126-139) reports Http2 only with SslStream ALPN ('never on Unity's runtimes') or the opt-in BouncyCastle provider; README.md:12 and Documentation~/Modules/Transport.md:20-21 say the same; there is no h2c or prior-knowledge path (only the remark at Http2Connection.cs:52). So in the default configuration the selection is a runtime branch the linker cannot cut and the code cannot execute. This is a size and modularity cost of a deliberate single-assembly design, not wrong behaviour; nothing tracks it (#429 is about a native ALPN backend, not about separating the stack).

Also reported as `http2-design-01`, `net-design-07` (merged into this issue).

Related: #258, #429, [[R11-pkg-pluggability-11]], [[R11-pkg-pluggability-02]].

title: [Packaging] Transport/link.xml preserves all members of List`1, ManualResetValueTaskSourceCore`1 and the System.Net.Security types for every build
body:
## Summary
Runtime/Transport/link.xml preserves open generic List`1 and several SslStream-related types with preserve="all", although the code reaches them through static call sites that the linker already keeps. Preserving the whole template forces IL2CPP to keep all members for every instantiation in the game. Build size grows for every user at Medium or High stripping.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/link.xml:53`

## Problem
Runtime/Transport/link.xml:52-55 '<type fullname="System.Collections.Generic.List`1" preserve="all"/>' and ManualResetValueTaskSourceCore`1; :15-19 preserve SslStream, SslClientAuthenticationOptions and SslApplicationProtocol 'all'. The file's comments say the provider 'calls them statically (no reflection since #303), so the linker already keeps what it uses; these rules stay as defense in depth' (:6-7) and that the List<SslApplicationProtocol> instantiation comes from 'a static call site' (:46-48). That call site uses only the List constructor and Add (Runtime/Transport/Tls/SslStreamTlsProvider.cs:348-355); a statically called member is never removed by UnityLinker, so preserving the open template adds nothing for it. The rule is applied in every stripped build (finding 01) and Tests/Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessorTests.cs:82 asserts it.

**Failure scenario.** In an IL2CPP build at Medium or High stripping the linker must keep all members of List<T> and its Enumerator, not just those the application uses; IL2CPP then emits them for the shared reference instantiation and for every value-type instantiation in the game (List<int>, List<Vector3>, ...). The same applies to SslStream's server-side and legacy overloads. The size is application dependent; a linker report diff with and without Transport/link.xml:52-55 on a real project would quantify it.

## Suggested fix
Remove the List`1, ManualResetValueTaskSourceCore`1 and the three System.Net.Security rules (keep the #450 configuration rules, which protect real reflection), and delete the matching assertions in TurboHttpLinkerProcessorTests. If a specific SslStream member is reached only by name inside Mono, preserve that member by signature.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The List`1, ManualResetValueTaskSourceCore`1, SslStream, SslClientAuthenticationOptions and SslApplicationProtocol preserve="all" rules are removed; the #450 configuration rules stay
- [ ] Matching assertions in TurboHttpLinkerProcessorTests are removed or updated
- [ ] A stripped IL2CPP build at High stripping still completes a TLS request, validated and recorded
- [ ] Linker report size difference with and without the rules is measured and noted in the PR

## Context

title: [Packaging] TurboHTTP.Complete cannot be excluded from a package install and drags WebSocket, JSON and Testing references into every player
body:
## Summary
TurboHTTP.Complete is auto-referenced with no define constraint and AlwaysLinkAssembly, so a consumer of an immutable UPM package has no way to exclude it, although the docs describe a lean path that excludes it. Its bootstrap statically references the WebSocket transport, JSON and JsonUtility, and 10 of its 15 asmdef references, including TurboHTTP.Testing, are unused. Size-sensitive projects ship WebSocket code they never use.

## Location
- `Runtime/TurboHTTP.Complete.asmdef:27`

## Problem
Runtime/TurboHTTP.Complete.asmdef:27 has 'defineConstraints: []' and :26 'autoReferenced: true'; Runtime/Bootstrap/AssemblyInfo.cs:8 adds [assembly: AlwaysLinkAssembly] and TurboHttpBootstrap is [Preserve] with two [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod] methods (TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:31-50, 82-91). A UPM package from a Git URL or registry is immutable, so a consumer has no define, setting or link.xml that removes this assembly; yet the 'projects that exclude TurboHTTP.Complete call EnsureRegistered themselves' path is documented in TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:27-29, RawSocketTransport.cs:81-83, RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:48-50, JsonModuleRegistration.cs:12-17, ProjectJsonBridge.cs:8-10, Documentation~/APIReference.md:199-202 and Development~/docs/agents/architecture.md:70-72. No document says how to exclude it and no test compiles or runs without it (DefaultTransportRegistrationTests only call EnsureRegistered with Complete present). The bootstrap calls RawSocketWebSocketTransport.EnsureRegistered() (TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:54), JsonModuleRegistration.EnsureRegistered() and JsonUtilitySerializer.RegisterAsDefaultIfBuiltIn() (:89-90) unconditionally, so Complete.dll references TurboHTTP.WebSocket.Transport, TurboHTTP.WebSocket (IWebSocketTransport), TurboHTTP.JSON and UnityEngine.JSONSerializeModule. At stripping levels that remove unreachable members this keeps about 1 KLOC of WebSocket code; at Minimal (assemblies in the closure are copied whole) it keeps the entire TurboHTTP.WebSocket assembly: 36 files, 10,556 lines, 64 types, for a project that never opens a WebSocket. The source under Runtime/Bootstrap uses only TurboHTTP.Core, .JSON, .JSON.Lite, .Transport and .WebSocket.Transport (usings at TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:1-7, JsonUtilitySerializer.cs:1-11); the asmdef (:4-20) also lists Unity.WebSocket, Retry, Cache, Auth, Observability, Files, Unity, Testing (:16), RateLimit and Middleware. asmdef references are not transitive (stated in Tests/Editor/ModuleAutoReferenceTests.cs:10-13), so these ten edges give consumers nothing; Tools~/ci/check_repo.py:57 allows Complete any reference (None), which is why a runtime assembly referencing the test-double module passes. The asmdef also sits at Runtime/ root, so any .cs later added outside a module folder silently joins the always-linked assembly.

**Failure scenario.** A size-sensitive mobile project wants HTTP/1.1 + its own Newtonsoft serializer and no WebSocket. It installs the package by Git URL: TurboHTTP.Complete is compiled, always linked and registers the WebSocket transport, the JSON bridge and JsonUtilitySerializer at SubsystemRegistration. The only way to reach the documented lean path is to embed a copy of the package and delete Runtime/Bootstrap and the asmdef; once done, nothing tells the user that the Android cleartext platform policy (finding 03) has no public registration call either.

## Suggested fix
Give Complete an opt-out the consumer can set without editing the package: defineConstraints ['!TURBOHTTP_NO_BOOTSTRAP'] (Unity 2021.3 supports negated constraints), or split the WebSocket registration into its own tiny bootstrap gated the same way. Cut the asmdef references to Core, Transport, JSON, WebSocket, WebSocket.Transport and make check_repo enforce that list (and forbid Testing). Move the asmdef into Runtime/Bootstrap/. Add a shadow-build variant or EditMode test that compiles with the opt-out define and exercises the three EnsureRegistered calls, and document the lean setup in one place.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] TurboHTTP.Complete can be disabled by a consumer-settable define (for example defineConstraints ['!TURBOHTTP_NO_BOOTSTRAP']) or the WebSocket registration is split into its own gated bootstrap
- [ ] The asmdef references are reduced to Core, Transport, JSON, WebSocket and WebSocket.Transport; check_repo.py enforces that list and forbids TurboHTTP.Testing
- [ ] The lean setup is documented in one place
- [ ] Test in Tests/Runtime/Core/ or a shadow-build variant compiles with the opt-out define and exercises the three EnsureRegistered calls, failing before the change

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `pkg-pluggability-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/pkg.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Runtime/TurboHTTP.Complete.asmdef:26-27 has autoReferenced true and defineConstraints []; Runtime/Bootstrap/AssemblyInfo.cs:8 is [assembly: AlwaysLinkAssembly]; TurboHttpBootstrap is [Preserve] with two SubsystemRegistration hooks (TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:31, 45-50, 82-87) that call RawSocketTransport.EnsureRegistered, RawSocketWebSocketTransport.EnsureRegistered, JsonModuleRegistration.EnsureRegistered and JsonUtilitySerializer.RegisterAsDefaultIfBuiltIn unconditionally (:53-54, :89-90). No define, setting or constraint lets a consumer drop the assembly from an immutable install; the only route is an embedded copy with the asmdef deleted. The 'projects that exclude TurboHTTP.Complete' path is documented at TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:27-29, RawSocketTransport.cs:81-83, RawSocketWebSocketTransport.cs:48-50, JsonModuleRegistration.cs:12-16, ProjectJsonBridge.cs:8-9, APIReference.md:199-202 and architecture.md:70-72, with no instruction how to exclude it. Tools~/ci/shadow_build.py has no variant without Complete. Sources under Runtime/Bootstrap use only Core, JSON, Transport, WebSocket.Transport (plus WebSocket for the interface) while the asmdef lists 15 references including TurboHTTP.Testing; check_repo.py:57 allows any (None). The journal build confirms unused asmdef references emit nothing (ManagedStripped has no Cache/Files/Testing, 2026-11-player-build-smoke.md:67), so the 10 extra edges are harmless clutter (low on their own); architecture.md:32 documents them as an 'aggregation asmdef', although ModuleAutoReferenceTests.cs:10-13 states an aggregate cannot re-export modules. Counts check: Runtime/WebSocket is 36 files, 10,556 lines. The asmdef sits at Runtime/ root and Runtime/Bootstrap has no asmdef of its own. #187 (fold WebSocket.Transport into Transport) is a different change and does not track this.

title: [Mobile] Android cleartext platform policy is installed by a private startup hook in TurboHTTP.Unity that is not rooted against stripping
body:
## Summary
AndroidCleartextTrafficPolicy.Install is a private RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod in the optional TurboHTTP.Unity assembly, which has no AlwaysLinkAssembly. It survives stripping only because the unrelated decoder link.xml roots the assembly. If the hook does not run, CleartextTrafficPolicy.IsPermitted returns true for any host once AllowCleartext is true, contradicting the documented behaviour on Android.

## Location
- `Runtime/Unity/Mobile/Android/AndroidCleartextTrafficPolicy.cs:28`

## Problem
AndroidCleartextTrafficPolicy.Install is 'private static' with only [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(SubsystemRegistration)] (AndroidCleartextTrafficPolicy.cs:25-33) inside an 'internal static class' (:21) of TurboHTTP.Unity. Runtime/Unity/AssemblyInfo.cs has only InternalsVisibleTo; the only [assembly: AlwaysLinkAssembly] are in Runtime/Bootstrap/AssemblyInfo.cs:8 and Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/AssemblyInfo.cs:6, both with comments explaining that an unreferenced package assembly is otherwise skipped by UnityLinker and its hooks never run. TurboHTTP.Complete does not reference any TurboHTTP.Unity type (TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:1-7), so in a project whose scripts use only Core/Transport the single thing that makes UnityLinker process TurboHTTP.Unity is Runtime/Unity/link.xml (decoder types), delivered through TurboHttpLinkerProcessor. When the hook does not run, CleartextTrafficPolicy.PlatformPolicy stays null and CleartextTrafficPolicy.IsPermitted returns true for any host once AllowCleartext is true (Runtime/Core/CleartextTrafficPolicy.cs:70-74: 'if (platformPolicy == null) return true'). The documentation promises the opposite: 'TurboHTTP refuses it unless AllowCleartext = true and the app's policy permits the host' (Documentation~/PlatformNotes.md:168-172), and Core's own doc says 'On Android players the TurboHTTP Unity module installs a platform policy' (CleartextTrafficPolicy.cs:23-24). No test asserts the root (compare TransportBootstrapTests.cs:45-64, which does assert [Preserve] and AlwaysLinkAssembly for the transport bootstrap).

**Failure scenario.** Someone removes the decoder rules from Runtime/Unity/link.xml (the obvious clean-up, see finding 01 and #158), or a project copies the package without the Editor assembly so the linker processor does not run. An Android IL2CPP app that uses only UHttpClient with AllowCleartext = true and a network security config permitting cleartext for one debug host now sends http:// to every host: TurboHTTP.Unity is not processed by the linker, Install never runs, and the platform check silently disappears. Confirm with a stripped Android player whose scripts reference no TurboHTTP.Unity type: log CleartextTrafficPolicy.PlatformPolicy != null at startup with and without the Unity link.xml.

## Suggested fix
Give the security hook an explicit root that does not depend on other modules' rules: install the Android policy from the TurboHTTP.Complete bootstrap (already UnityEngine-aware and always linked) through a small registration API, or mark TurboHTTP.Unity [assembly: AlwaysLinkAssembly] with [Preserve] on Install and accept that cost knowingly. Expose a public EnsureRegistered for lean builds, and add a test like TransportBootstrapTests that fails if the root is removed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The Android policy install is rooted independently of other modules' link.xml rules (installed from the Complete bootstrap through a registration API, or via AlwaysLinkAssembly and Preserve on Install)
- [ ] A public EnsureRegistered exists for lean builds
- [ ] A test like TransportBootstrapTests in Tests/Runtime/Unity/ fails if the root is removed
- [ ] Stripped Android IL2CPP player with scripts referencing no TurboHTTP.Unity type logs PlatformPolicy != null, validated on a device and recorded

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `pkg-pluggability-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/pkg.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: Code is as described. AndroidCleartextTrafficPolicy.Install is private static with only [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(SubsystemRegistration)] inside an internal static class (Runtime/Unity/Mobile/Android/AndroidCleartextTrafficPolicy.cs:21-33); Runtime/Unity/AssemblyInfo.cs has only InternalsVisibleTo; the only AlwaysLinkAssembly attributes are Runtime/Bootstrap/AssemblyInfo.cs:8 and Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/AssemblyInfo.cs:6; nothing in Runtime/Bootstrap references a TurboHTTP.Unity type. CleartextTrafficPolicy.IsPermitted returns true when no platform policy is installed and AllowCleartext is true (Runtime/Core/CleartextTrafficPolicy.cs:70-74), so a hook that never runs fails open, against PlatformNotes.md:168-172 and CleartextTrafficPolicy.cs:23-24. No test asserts the root: the only tests touching the Android policy are the Resolve/cache tests in Tests/Runtime/Mobile/AndroidJniThreadTests.cs:150-213. The repo's own build record shows the risk is real: at Stripping High an unreferenced package assembly with a [Preserve] startup hook (TurboHTTP.Observability) is absent from the linker output (2026-11-player-build-smoke.md:67), so in a project whose scripts use no TurboHTTP.Unity type the hook depends on Runtime/Unity/link.xml (decoder rules) reaching UnityLinker and on UnityLinker then honouring the hook attribute in that assembly. Neither is recorded for a Core-only project (the smoke project uses TurboHTTP.Unity), so today's state is unverified rather than shown broken; the stated failure needs the decoder rules removed or the linker processor absent. Impact is bounded: AllowCleartext defaults to false on Android players (CleartextTrafficPolicy.cs:29-33), so only apps that opted in and rely on a per-host network security config are exposed. The built-in Android policy has no public install call (IsCleartextTrafficPermitted is internal), though CleartextTrafficPolicy.PlatformPolicy itself is a public setter.

Also reported as `unity-design-05` (merged into this issue).

Related: [[R11-pkg-pluggability-02]].

title: [CI] BannedSymbols.txt lists only one overload of each IL2CPP-unsafe API, leaving Activator.CreateInstance<T>, Type.GetType, Assembly.Load and UnityWebRequest unguarded

## Summary
BannedSymbols.txt bans one Activator.CreateInstance overload and the MakeGeneric APIs, but RS0030 matches exact documentation ids, so other overloads, Type.GetType(string), Assembly.Load and UnityWebRequest pass the shadow build. CLAUDE.md states that banned APIs fail the build. Current sources are clean, so the gap is only in the guard.

## Location
- `Tools~/ci/BannedSymbols.txt:11`

## Problem
Tools~/ci/BannedSymbols.txt:11 lists only 'M:System.Activator.CreateInstance(System.Type)'; :9-10 list MethodInfo.MakeGenericMethod and Type.MakeGenericType; :32-34 ban HttpClient, WebClient and HttpWebRequest. RS0030 matches exact documentation ids, so Activator.CreateInstance<T>() (also what a 'new()' constraint compiles to), CreateInstance(Type, bool) and CreateInstance(Type, params object[]), Type.GetType(string) (the by-name lookup #186 removed; check_reflect in check_repo.py:284-299 only catches assembly-qualified TurboHTTP names), Assembly.Load/GetTypes and UnityEngine.Networking.UnityWebRequest (CLAUDE.md section 3: the main transport never uses it) are all allowed. The current sources are clean: the only reflection under Runtime/ outside Lib/ is JsonUtilitySerializer.cs:362 and IL2CPPCompatibility.cs:91, so the gap is purely in the guard.

**Failure scenario.** New code in a module creates a handler with Activator.CreateInstance(type, args) or resolves Type.GetType("MyGame.Dto"). The shadow build passes; under Managed Stripping Level High on a device the constructor or type is gone and the call throws MissingMethodException or returns null, which CI was supposed to prevent.

## Suggested fix
Add the remaining Activator.CreateInstance overloads (including the generic one), Type.GetType(System.String) and its overloads, Assembly.Load*, and T:UnityEngine.Networking.UnityWebRequest with an explicit allowance for AudioClipHandler's file:// decode in the analyzer baseline.

title: [CI] check_repo.py does not enforce asmdef define constraints, autoReferenced, platform excludes or the native plugin gate list
body:
## Summary
check_asmdef validates only reference names, unsafe and noEngineReferences. Define constraints, autoReferenced, excludePlatforms and plugin gating are pinned only by Unity EditMode tests that PR CI does not run, and the shadow build always defines the gating symbols. A refactor can drop the BouncyCastle define constraint and ship the TLS stack in every build while CI stays green.

## Location
- `Tools~/ci/check_repo.py:110`

## Problem
check_asmdef (Tools~/ci/check_repo.py:110-138) validates references against ALLOWED_REFS, GUID references, allowUnsafeCode and noEngineReferences, nothing else. The rules that decide what reaches a player live in Tests/Editor/ModuleAutoReferenceTests.cs (autoReferenced per module :45-72, the BouncyCastle define constraint :74-81, the UniTask constraints :83-97) and Tests/Editor/BackgroundPluginPackagingTests.cs (:74-82, gate covers both plugins). CLAUDE.md section 5 and .github/workflows/ci.yml:146 state that CI never runs Unity tests (#188). The shadow build cannot notice a lost constraint because it always defines TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE and UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS (Tools~/ci/shadow_build.py:71-76). Further gaps in the same file: ALLOWED_REFS maps TurboHTTP.Complete to None (:57) although architecture.md lists exactly 15 references and says it omits BouncyCastle and UniTask; check_native models PluginImporter defineConstraints as effective (:594) while TurboHttpBackgroundPluginGate.cs:16-19 records that Unity 2021.3 ignores them for native plugins, so real inclusion depends on the C# GatedPluginPaths list (:29-33), which the check never reads; NATIVE_SOURCES (:497) excludes .androidlib, so the Android plugin's gating is unchecked; check_reflect (:284-299) matches only assembly-qualified strings; the samples check (:659-664) does not flag a Samples~ folder with an asmdef that package.json does not list.

**Failure scenario.** A refactor rewrites TurboHTTP.Transport.BouncyCastle.asmdef and drops 'defineConstraints'. check.sh and PR CI stay green (references unchanged, shadow build defines the symbol anyway). Every customer build now compiles the glue, which is [AlwaysLinkAssembly] with a startup registration, so the whole BouncyCastle TLS stack is linked into all players until the next periodic host-editor run happens to execute ModuleAutoReferenceTests. The same holds for removing UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS from a test asmdef or adding a third native plugin with a meta constraint but no entry in GatedPluginPaths.

## Suggested fix
Move the asmdef invariants into check_repo.py as data: per assembly the expected defineConstraints, autoReferenced, excludePlatforms and (for Complete) the exact reference list; require UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS on every asmdef under Tests/; require that an assembly excludes every platform that one of its references excludes. Make check_native read GatedPluginPaths and treat .androidlib folders as plugins. Keep the EditMode tests as the Unity-side confirmation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] check_repo.py checks per assembly the expected defineConstraints, autoReferenced and excludePlatforms, the exact TurboHTTP.Complete reference list, and UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS on every Tests/ asmdef
- [ ] check_native reads GatedPluginPaths and treats .androidlib folders as plugins
- [ ] check_repo.py self-test or fixture fails when the BouncyCastle asmdef loses its defineConstraints, failing before the change
- [ ] The Unity EditMode tests stay as the Unity-side confirmation

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `pkg-pluggability-10` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/pkg.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Not independently verified: low-severity findings were not sent to a second reviewer. Re-trace it in the code before fixing.

Related: #188, [[R11-pkg-pluggability-02]], [[R11-pkg-pluggability-09]].

title: [Packaging] package.json declares no com.unity.modules dependencies although TurboHTTP.Unity and Complete use five built-in engine modules
body:
## Summary
package.json has an empty dependencies object while TurboHTTP.Unity uses UnityWebRequest, UnityWebRequestAudio, Audio, ImageConversion and AndroidJNI, and TurboHTTP.Complete uses JsonUtility. A project that disabled one of those modules gets compile errors inside the immutable package with no dependency hint in Package Manager. Declared dependencies would make Unity re-enable the modules.

## Location
- `package.json:31`

## Problem
package.json:31 'dependencies: {}'. TurboHTTP.Unity (noEngineReferences: false, compiled for every platform, no constraints) uses UnityWebRequestMultimedia.GetAudioClip and UnityWebRequest.Result (Runtime/Unity/AudioClipHandler.cs:9, 418, 445: com.unity.modules.unitywebrequest, .unitywebrequestaudio, .audio), Texture2D.LoadImage (Runtime/Unity/Texture2DHandler.cs:522: com.unity.modules.imageconversion) and AndroidJavaClass/AndroidJNI (8 + 8 uses under Runtime/Unity/Mobile/Android: com.unity.modules.androidjni); TurboHTTP.Complete uses JsonUtility (Runtime/Bootstrap/JsonUtilitySerializer.cs:197, 268: com.unity.modules.jsonserialize). The BouncyCastle glue also uses AndroidJNI (Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/AndroidTrustManagerVerifier.cs). Tools~/ci/check_repo.py:151-154 checks only that name, version, displayName, unity and description exist.

**Failure scenario.** A mobile team trims built-in packages to cut engine size and disables 'Unity Web Request Audio' (or Audio, Image Conversion, JSON Serialize). After adding com.turbohttp.complete the project stops compiling with CS0246/CS0103 in Runtime/Unity/AudioClipHandler.cs (or Texture2DHandler.cs, JsonUtilitySerializer.cs) inside Library/PackageCache, where they cannot edit; Package Manager shows no dependency to explain it. With declared dependencies Unity would re-enable the modules automatically. The flip side is the size cost: because the whole Unity module is one assembly, wanting only the coroutine wrapper or the dispatcher forces Audio, UnityWebRequest, UnityWebRequestAudio and ImageConversion to stay enabled.

## Suggested fix
Declare the com.unity.modules.* packages the shipped assemblies use in package.json, and add a check_repo rule that maps the engine namespaces used under Runtime/ to declared modules. To let size-conscious projects drop Audio and UnityWebRequest, split the audio pipeline (AudioClipHandler, StreamedAudioTempFiles, audio decoders) into TurboHTTP.Unity.Audio so the core Unity module needs only ImageConversion and AndroidJNI.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] package.json declares every com.unity.modules.* package used by shipped assemblies (unitywebrequest, unitywebrequestaudio, audio, imageconversion, androidjni, jsonserialize)
- [ ] check_repo.py maps engine namespaces used under Runtime/ to declared modules and fails on a missing one
- [ ] Optionally the audio pipeline is split into TurboHTTP.Unity.Audio so lean projects can drop Audio and UnityWebRequest
- [ ] Check in Tools~/ci is exercised by a fixture that fails before the change

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `pkg-pluggability-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/pkg.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: platform-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: package.json has "dependencies": {} while shipped assemblies use built-in engine modules with no #if or versionDefines guard: TurboHTTP.Unity (Runtime/Unity/TurboHTTP.Unity.asmdef: noEngineReferences false, no constraints, versionDefines []) calls UnityWebRequestMultimedia.GetAudioClip and UnityWebRequest.Result (Runtime/Unity/AudioClipHandler.cs:418, 445), Texture2D.LoadImage (Runtime/Unity/Texture2DHandler.cs:522) and AndroidJavaClass (AndroidCleartextTrafficPolicy.cs:100-108, AndroidJniThread.cs, AndroidBackgroundPluginJni.cs); TurboHTTP.Complete calls JsonUtility (Runtime/Bootstrap/JsonUtilitySerializer.cs:197). Tools~/ci/check_repo.py:150-153 checks only name, version, displayName, unity and description. No com.unity.modules.* dependency is declared anywhere in the package. A project with one of those built-in modules disabled gets compile errors inside the package, which a declared dependency would prevent. Edge configuration (modules are on by default), but the break is a hard compile failure in an immutable package and the fix is a manifest edit. #101 (Asset Store packaging) does not mention dependencies.

Also reported as `unity-design-03` (merged into this issue).

Related: #101, [[R11-pkg-pluggability-10]].
